approbation

ap-ruh-BAY-shun · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Approbation is praise or admiring approval, especially official or enthusiastic.

The young violinist's flawless performance earned the approbation of even the harshest critics in the audience.

Example

The board's approbation of the new safety plan meant it could move forward without further review.

Approbation is more than just liking something -- it's an official or emphatic seal of approval.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

approval: Approval is the official yes -- agreement that something is acceptable and may go ahead -- and it can be given coolly, with no delight at all. Approbation is approval that glows: it adds open admiration and praise to the bare permission.

commendation: A commendation is a formal act of praise for a particular piece of good work -- a citation, a medal, a public thank-you. Approbation is the warm, admiring attitude such gestures express; you can sense a critic's approbation before any award is ever given.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

disapproval: a negative judgment or feeling

condemnation: strong formal criticism or disapproval

Where it sits · how glowing the reception is — acceptance → approbation → adulation

acceptance vs. approbation: Acceptance is much cooler than approbation -- a basic willingness to let something stand, with no praise attached, while approbation beams with admiring, enthusiastic approval.

adulation vs. approbation: Adulation is excessive, worshipful admiration -- even more intense than approbation.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — ap-

prefix — ap-: variant of ad-, 'to, toward' (Latin)

root — probation

root — probation: a real modern English word: a trial or supervised testing period (shares the Latin root probare, 'to test, prove, approve') (Latin probare)

Put it together

Put it together: Approbation comes from Latin ap- ('to') + probare ('to test, prove, approve') -- the same root behind probation. Literally, it's the result of something being 'tested and approved.'

Use the root in a new word: probation

Use the root in a new word: probation: After one late assignment too many, the intern was placed on probation for the rest of the semester.

Word Choice

Approbation is a formal word for enthusiastic approval, often from someone in a position of authority -- reserve it for situations more official than casual, everyday praise.
